Concurrency target: cap 400 simultaneous active sessions for chat endpoints (avg 30 tokens response). sla_negotiation_summary: SLA asks: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 64-token responses at committed throughput; p99 <= 350ms. Minimum tokens/sec guaranteed at pool level (not per-VIP). Remedies: service credit equal to 5% of monthly committed fee per SLA breach event, escalated to 10% if repeat within same month. Redwood asked for monitoring hooks (per-route token-level metrics + traces) and 12-hour RCA window. Customer wants ability to test under load and acceptance criteria defined by POC (throughput sustained 90% of target for 24h with no p95 breaches). Negotiation point: customer insists on hard concurrency caps enforced by Redwood to prevent noisy neighbors; Redwood proposes soft reservations + strict burst gating. Legal is pushing for explicit credit caps and termination right if monthly breaches >3.
